name: dcf-aapl-2026-09-12
description: Illustrative AAPL-shaped context for tests. Statement figures are approximate; the news items and the model reply are synthetic and were written by hand because no API key was available when this fixture was created. Re-record against the live API with `npm run fixtures:record`.

profile.name: Apple Inc.
profile.description: Designs and sells smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells related services including the App Store, cloud storage, payments and subscriptions.

news.title: Apple unveils iPhone 18 lineup, keeps base prices flat
news.summary: Apple introduced four iPhone 18 models at its September event and held US starting prices unchanged from last year, while raising the Pro Max price by $100.

news.title: EU regulators open formal review of Apple App Store fee changes
news.summary: The European Commission opened a formal review into whether Apple's revised App Store terms comply with the Digital Markets Act, a process that can end in fines of up to 10% of global turnover.

news.title: 3 reasons Apple stock could soar this fall
news.summary: An opinion piece arguing new devices and services growth could lift the shares.

news.title: Apple in talks to expand Gemini partnership for Siri
news.summary: People familiar with the matter said Apple is negotiating a multi-year extension of its agreement to use Google's Gemini models in Siri. Terms were not disclosed and no deal has been signed.

news.title: Apple shares rise 2% as tech stocks rebound
news.summary: Apple rose alongside other large technology names as bond yields fell.

news.title: US judge sets 2027 trial date in DOJ antitrust case against Apple
news.summary: A federal judge scheduled the Justice Department's antitrust case against Apple for trial beginning in March 2027.

news.title: TSMC begins volume production of Apple A20 chips on 2nm
news.summary: TSMC started volume production of Apple's A20 processor on its 2-nanometer process, according to people familiar with the schedule.

news.title: Apple reports third quarter results
news.summary: Apple reported quarterly revenue of $97.9 billion, up 4 percent year over year, with Services revenue at an all-time high of $28.9 billion. The board declared a dividend of $0.27 per share.

modelOutput.headline: The valuation rests on continued double digit revenue acceleration against a five year record of low single digit growth, discounted at a modest rate.
modelOutput.plainEnglish: This estimate assumes Apple's growth picks up notably from its recent pace and that its cost of capital stays low. If growth instead tracks its five year average, the fair value would likely be lower.
modelOutput.inputRationale: This review applies to the displayed intrinsic value of $198.50, which is the engine's pure discounted cash flow output.

assumptions.evidence: Revenue growth per year across five periods is 3.28%, though trailing twelve month revenue is up 5.8% versus the last fiscal year; free cash flow growth per year is 1.54%.
assumptions.reasoning: 7.00% stage 1 growth is well above both the multi year revenue trend and the recent uptick, and far above historic free cash flow growth.

assumptions.evidence: Terminal growth is 2.50% against an 8.40% discount rate, and terminal value is 71% of enterprise value per the engine's own confidence note.
assumptions.reasoning: 2.50% is a reasonable long run assumption, but the narrow 5.9 point gap to WACC combined with the 71% terminal value share means the result depends heavily on the terminal assumptions.

assumptions.evidence: Debt to equity is 1.38x, net debt to EBITDA is 0.45x, no sovereign backstop is on file, and the company has a $3.51T market cap with 58.2% return on invested capital.
assumptions.reasoning: 8.40% seems reasonable to slightly low for a company of this size and financial strength with no sovereign backstop, sitting near the lower end of what a large, stable but non-guaranteed issuer would warrant.

assumptions.evidence: Engine uses $98.80B, matching the last fiscal year's free cash flow, while trailing twelve month free cash flow is $116.60B and stock compensation is 13.1% of latest free cash flow.
assumptions.reasoning: The engine's base is actually below the more current trailing twelve month figure, so it is conservative rather than inflated relative to recent performance.

dominantSensitivity.explanation: With terminal value already 71% of enterprise value and only a 5.9 point spread between WACC and terminal growth, small changes to either the terminal growth rate or the discount rate swing the valuation substantially more than changes to stage 1 growth.

confidenceReasons: Stage 1 growth of 7% is notably above the five year revenue and free cash flow trend, though closer to the recent trailing twelve month uptick.
Terminal value dominates the calculation at 71% of enterprise value, per the engine's own flagged weakness.
Five annual periods provide a reasonably solid but not extensive historical base for judgment.
Financial strength metrics such as low net debt to EBITDA and high return on invested capital support a stable discount rate assumption.
